content.text: Succession voting is a feature of six succession methods: Elective gavelkind , Tanistry , Eldership , Feudal elective , Princely elective , and Imperial elective .
The succession law determines the voters, the possible candidates, and even how AI voters evaluate candidates.

content.text: Most voters will vote for the candidate to whom they assign the highest score. However, a voter who is nominated by the ruler will usually vote for themselves (accepting the nomination), while members of claimant factions will often vote for their preferred claimant.
This section lists score modifiers for Feudal elective . The table above summarizes the ways in which other succession laws cause different voting behavior.

content.text: Voters prefer to elect their relatives. The ruler is especially interested in electing their children. The ruler also tends to nominate their dynastic heir (except under Eldership): when their dynasty is winning, they will avoid switching nominees or splitting on different titles.

content.text: Each succession law has its own age preferences. Voters will not judge themselves on age.
Feudal Elective voters prefer adults who aren't too old, and especially adults close in age to the voter:
Voters prefer candidates of the same culture , especially if they share the ruler's culture. Culturism is more important for tribal/dynastic succession laws (Elective Gavelkind, Tanistry, Eldership).

sections.heading: Warrior values, diplomatic values, and spiritual values

content.text: Characters will vote according to "warrior values", "diplomatic values", or "spiritual values" depending on their religion and government. [1]
If Holy Fury is not enabled, reformed pagan religions apply the same values as the corresponding old religion.
